display.text:
name: Android APK Build

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'code/**'
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  build-apk:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write

    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up JDK 17
        uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with:
          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: '17'

      - name: Cache Gradle
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.gradle/caches
            ~/.gradle/wrapper
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-gradle-${{ hashFiles('code/gradle.properties', 'code/gradle-wrapper.jar') }}

      - name: Grant execute permission for gradlew
        run: chmod +x code/gradlew

      - name: Build Debug APK
        working-directory: code
        run: ./gradlew assembleDebug

      - name: Upload Debug APK
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: zen-panel-debug-apk
          path: code/app/build/outputs/apk/debug/*.apk

      - name: Build Release APK
        working-directory: code
        run: |
          echo "Keystore not configured - skipping release build"
          echo "To build release, add keystore to code/keystore/ and set properties in gradle.properties"

      - name: Release Please (optional)
        if: false
        run: |
          echo "Create GitHub Release manually or configure release-please"

Let me explain both options concretely in terms of this specific app (Zen Panel).

Option A — full native Kotlin UI (classic Views/Material): 
- MainActivity native screen with cards: features list, search box, status, buttons.
- Uses ConnectivityManager for online/offline, NotificationManager/NotificationCompat for push with POST_NOTIFICATIONS permission, SharedPreferences for storage and traffic log, Intent ACTION_VIEW to open Google search, second Activity as extension simulator.
- No WebView; UI built in XML + Kotlin.
- Result: a normal Android app, APK ~ a few MB, no HTML.
- Pros: fast, looks/feels native, no browser dependency, works offline, easy Play-style packaging. Cons: UI is a re-creation, not pixel-identical to PWA; any new PWA feature must be re-implemented.

Option B — WebView wrapper over the existing PWA:
- Single Activity with a WebView. PWA files copied into app/src/main/assets/www, loaded via WebViewAssetLoader (https://appassets.androidplatform.net) so service worker / relative paths work.
- A JS bridge (addJavascriptInterface) exposes native functions: showNotification, getNetworkStatus, toggleBrowsec, openSearch.
- Extension simulator stays a page inside the WebView.
- Result: APK that looks exactly like the PWA inside an app shell; native Android handles notifications/permissions.
- Pros: fast to build, 1:1 with PWA, easy to update (edit HTML). Cons: hybrid, not "true" native; WebView perf; some PWA APIs (service worker) finicky.

I should also mention what the app does (features) since they asked "что из себя приложение представляет". And maybe note that the app itself is small — a panel mock: features list, Google search, notifications test, browsec toggle, extension simulator. No real VNC/terminals/git despite release notes.

Никаких VNC/терминалов/файлового менеджера/GitHub API в коде нет — это только в тексте описания релиза.

Так выглядят два моих варианта:

## Вариант A — полностью нативный (Kotlin, без WebView)
Обычное Android-приложение: UI собран из XML + Material-компонентов (карточки, поля, кнопки), логика на Kotlin.

- Онлайн/офлайн → `ConnectivityManager` + `registerDefaultNetworkCallback`.
- Уведомления → `NotificationManager`/`NotificationCompat`, запрос `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` на Android 13+.
- Хранилище + журнал трафика → `SharedPreferences`.
- Google-поиск → `Intent.ACTION_VIEW` (открывает браузер/приложение Google).
- «Расширение» → вторая нативная Activity-симулятор с поиском и списком результатов.
- Browsec → нативный переключатель-симуляция (сохраняется в prefs).

Итог: APK-приложение без HTML, быстрое, офлайновое, вид «как приложение», а не «как сайт». Минус: это пересоздание, а не пиксель-в-пиксель копия PWA; новые фичи PWA придётся повторять руками.

## Вариант B — WebView-обёртка над PWA
Одна нативная Activity, внутри `WebView`, который грузит те же PWA-файлы из `app/src/main/assets/www` через `WebViewAssetLoader` (чтобы работали относительные пути и service worker).

- Нативный слой даёт: системные уведомления, разрешения, статус сети, APK-обёртку, иконку, установку.
- JS↔Android мост (`addJavascriptInterface`): `showNotification`, `getNetworkStatus`, `openSearch`, `toggleBrowsec`.
- Симулятор расширения остаётся HTML-страницей внутри WebView.

Итог: APK выглядит ровно как PWA (1:1), собирается быстро, правки — в знакомом HTML/JS. Минус: это гибрид, а не «нативный» в строгом смысле; производительность WebView; service worker в WebView капризен.

## Главная развилка
- Хочешь «настоящий Android» с нативным UI → **A**.
- Хочешь быстро получить APK, идентичный PWA → **B**.

Actually, let me reconsider the architecture for a "provider-agnostic" client. The user wants country selection, speed, notifications, real traffic. WireGuard gives all that if we have configs.

Let me design the data model and storage:

`VpnProfile`:
- id (UUID)
- name
- country (String, e.g. "Netherlands")
- countryCode (for flag emoji maybe)
- config (WireGuard config text)

Stored as JSON in a file or SharedPreferences. I'll use a simple JSON via org.json (built-in) — no extra dependency.

UI:
- MainActivity: existing Zen Panel + a "VPN" card with:
  - status (connected/disconnected + country)
  - toggle button (connect/disconnect)
  - "Выбрать сервер" button → ServerListActivity
  - stats: ↓ speed, ↑ speed, total
  - "Добавить сервер" (import config)
- ServerListActivity: list of profiles with country, select, delete, add via paste/import.
- Add server: dialog to paste WireGuard config + name/country (or parse from config comments).

Service:
- `ZenVpnService extends VpnService` (because the WireGuard tunnel library requires a VpnService subclass). Use `GoBackend` from the library.
- Foreground service with notification (country + speed). Actually WireGuard's `GoBackend.VpnService` needs to be the service. We can subclass `GoBackend.VpnService` and override, or follow the official example.

The official WireGuard library usage:
```kotlin
class ZenVpnService : VpnService() {
    companion object {
        val backend: GoBackend by lazy { GoBackend(applicationContext) } // needs Application context
    }
    ...
}
```
Actually the library's `GoBackend` constructor takes a Context, and it manages the VpnService. The official Android app uses `class ZenVpnService : VpnService(), ...` and `GoBackend(this)`. Wait, GoBackend needs `applicationContext` and a `VpnService` instance. Let me recall the API:

From wireguard-android library:
- `com.wireguard.android.backend.GoBackend(context: Context)` 
- `GoBackend.VpnService` is a nested class? Actually the library provides `GoBackend.VpnService`? Let me recall.

The `tunnel` artifact provides:
- `com.wireguard.config.Config`, `Interface`, `Peer`, `InetNetwork`, `InetEndpoint`
- `com.wireguard.android.backend.GoBackend`, `com.wireguard.android.backend.Tunnel`, `com.wireguard.android.backend.Backend`, `State`
- `GoBackend.VpnService` — the library declares a `VpnService` subclass in its manifest: `<service android:name="com.wireguard.android.backend.GoBackend$VpnService" ... />`. Yes! The AAR manifest declares the VpnService. So we don't create our own VpnService; we use `GoBackend.VpnService` declared by the library. We need to add the service permission and `android:permission`? Let me recall: the library manifest has:
```xml
<service android:name="com.wireguard.android.backend.GoBackend$VpnService"
    android:permission="android.permission.BIND_VPN_SERVICE"
    android:exported="false">
    <intent-filter>
        <action android:name="android.net.VpnService"/>
    </intent-filter>
</service>
```
So manifest merger includes it automatically. We just need `<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.BIND_VPN_SERVICE"/>`? Actually BIND_VPN_SERVICE is a signature permission used to protect the service; the app declaring the service needs it? The library's own manifest likely includes it. Let me not worry; we may need to add it.

Usage:
```kotlin
val backend = GoBackend(applicationContext)
val tunnel = object : Tunnel { override fun getName() = "zen"; override fun onStateChange(newState: State) {...} }
val config = Config.parse(BufferedReader(FileInputStream(file)))  // or Config.parse(InputStream)
backend.setState(tunnel, State.UP, config)  // returns Config for VpnService.prepare? 
```
Actually `backend.setState(tunnel, State.UP, config)` where config type is `Config`. For prepare, the backend handles `VpnService.prepare` via an Intent. The library example:
```kotlin
val intent = VpnService.prepare(context)
if (intent != null) startActivityForResult(intent, REQUEST_CODE)
else backend.setState(tunnel, State.UP, config)
```

And statistics: `backend.getStatistics(tunnel)` returns `Statistics` with `totalRx`, `totalTx`, and possibly per-peer. Actually `getStatistics` may be deprecated; newer API: `backend.getStatistics(tunnel): Statistics`. Let me check version 1.0.20230706. There's `com.wireguard.android.backend.Statistics` with `totalRx`, `totalTx`. And `backend.getStatistics(tunnel)`.

Also `backend.getState(tunnel)`.

```java
public interface Tunnel {

    default String getName() { return "tunnel"; }

}
```

package com.zenpanel.app

import android.os.Bundle
import android.view.LayoutInflater
import android.widget.Toast
import androidx.appcompat.app.AppCompatActivity
import androidx.recyclerview.widget.LinearLayoutManager
import com.google.android.material.dialog.MaterialAlertDialogBuilder
import com.zenpanel.app.databinding.ActivityServerListBinding
import com.zenpanel.app.databinding.DialogAddServerBinding

class ServerListActivity : AppCompatActivity() {

    private lateinit var binding: ActivityServerListBinding
    private lateinit var app: App
    private lateinit var adapter: ServerAdapter

    override fun onCreate(savedInstanceState: Bundle?) {
        super.onCreate(savedInstanceState)
        binding = ActivityServerListBinding.inflate(layoutInflater)
        setContentView(binding.root)

        app = application as App

        binding.recyclerServers.layoutManager = LinearLayoutManager(this)
        render()

        binding.buttonAddServer.setOnClickListener { showAddDialog() }
    }

    private fun render() {
        val selectedId = app.servers.selectedId
        adapter = ServerAdapter(
            servers = app.servers.all(),
            selectedId = selectedId,
            onSelect = { server ->
                app.servers.selectedId = server.id
                render()
                toast(getString(R.string.server_selected, server.displayName()))
            },
            onDelete = { server ->
                app.servers.remove(server.id)
                render()
            }
        )
        binding.recyclerServers.adapter = adapter
        binding.textEmpty.visibility =
            if (app.servers.all().isEmpty()) android.view.View.VISIBLE else android.view.View.GONE
    }

    private fun showAddDialog() {
        val dialogBinding = DialogAddServerBinding.inflate(LayoutInflater.from(this))
        MaterialAlertDialogBuilder(this)
            .setTitle(R.string.server_add_title)
            .setView(dialogBinding.root)
            .setPositiveButton(R.string.server_add_save) { _, _ ->
                val config = dialogBinding.inputConfig.text?.toString()?.trim().orEmpty()
                if (config.isBlank()) {
                    toast(getString(R.string.server_config_required))
                    return@setPositiveButton
                }
                val countryCode = dialogBinding.inputCountryCode.text?.toString()?.trim().orEmpty()
                val server = VpnServer(
                    name = dialogBinding.inputName.text?.toString()?.trim().orEmpty()
                        .ifBlank { getString(R.string.server_default_name) },
                    country = dialogBinding.inputCountry.text?.toString()?.trim().orEmpty(),
                    countryCode = countryCode,
                    config = config
                )
                app.servers.add(server)
                render()
            }
            .setNegativeButton(R.string.close, null)
            .show()
    }

    private fun toast(message: String) {
        Toast.makeText(this, message, Toast.LENGTH_SHORT).show()
    }
}

name: Android APK Build

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'code/**'
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  build-apk:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write

    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up JDK 17
        uses: actions/setup-java@v4
        with:
          distribution: 'temurin'
          java-version: '17'

      - name: Set up Android SDK
        uses: android-actions/setup-android@v3

      - name: Cache Gradle
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.gradle/caches
            ~/.gradle/wrapper
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-gradle-${{ hashFiles('code/gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.properties', 'code/**/*.gradle.kts') }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-gradle-

      - name: Grant execute permission for gradlew
        run: chmod +x code/gradlew

      - name: Build Debug APK
        working-directory: code
        run: ./gradlew assembleDebug --stacktrace

      - name: Upload Debug APK
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: zen-panel-debug-apk
          path: code/app/build/outputs/apk/debug/*.apk

      - name: Build Release APK (unsigned)
        working-directory: code
        run: ./gradlew assembleRelease --stacktrace

      - name: Upload Release APK (unsigned)
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: zen-panel-release-apk-unsigned
          path: code/app/build/outputs/apk/release/*.apk

name: PWA Release

on:
  push:
    tags: ['v*']
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      version:
        description: 'Release version without leading v (e.g. 1.0.1)'
        required: true

jobs:
  create-release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write

    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Determine version
        id: ver
        run: |
          if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "workflow_dispatch" ]; then
            echo "version=${{ github.event.inputs.version }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "version=${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

      - name: Write release notes
        run: |
          cat > "$RUNNER_TEMP/release_notes.md" <<'EOF'
          ## Zen Panel

          ### Android app (native)
          - Native Kotlin UI (Material 3, dark theme)
          - Real VPN via WireGuard userspace backend (VpnService + route table)
          - Server list with country selection
          - Live traffic counters and speed, read from wireguard-go
          - Foreground notification with country and current speed
          - Google Search, network status and local traffic log
          - Extension simulator screen

          ### Install
          1. Download the APK artifact from the latest workflow run.
          2. Add your own WireGuard config in the app: Servers -> Add server.
          3. Pick a server and tap Connect.

          ### Layout
          - `pwa/` - static PWA files (manifest, service worker, HTML)
          - `code/` - native Android (Gradle) project
          EOF

      - name: Create GitHub Release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          gh release create "v${{ steps.ver.outputs.version }}" \
            --title "v${{ steps.ver.outputs.version }} - Zen Panel" \
            --notes-file "$RUNNER_TEMP/release_notes.md"

.gradle/
build/
local.properties
*.iml
.idea/
.cxx/
captures/
